title: Rydberg excitons in core-shell nanostructures II. Plasmon-exciton interaction and enhancement
authors: David Ziemkiewicz, Gerard Czajkowski, Sylwia Zielińska-Raczyńska
abstract: Interaction between Rydberg excitons in core-shell Cu$_2$O nanostructures and surface plasmons is investigated. An enhancement of a quadrupole transitions to the Rydberg exciton states in copper oxide plasmonic nanaostructures is examined. A possibility of a modification of plasmonic enhancment (i.e., an average amplification factor) of electric field distributions in the vicinity of nanostructures, which depends on its shape and geometrical size, is also discussed.
summary: This paper theoretically analyzes how surface plasmons enhance the weak quadrupole transitions of Rydberg excitons confined within core-shell nanostructures. By modeling the near-field enhancement and incorporating the large size of Rydberg excitons, the authors predict optimal structural dimensions that maximize this quantum optical effect.
main_problem: The paper investigates the enhancement of quadrupole transitions in Rydberg excitons due to their interaction with surface plasmons within core-shell nanostructures.
main_result: The plasmonic near-field significantly enhances these transitions, with optimal enhancement factors ($\eta$) observed at specific core radii ($\sim 80-100$ nm) that match the spatial scales of highly excited Rydberg states.
method: The study employs theoretical modeling combining near-field electrodynamics (FDTD/analytical solutions) with quantum mechanical descriptions of excitons, utilizing averaging techniques for large excitons.
model_or_system: The system involves core-shell nanostructures (e.g., Cu2O excitons) where the excitons interact with localized surface plasmons. The exciton states are modeled using modified Schrödinger-like equations leading to Whittaker equations.
key_observables:
Local field gradient ($
abla\vec{E}$), transition rate ($\gamma$) for quadrupole transitions, and the plasmonic amplification factor ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Rydberg principal quantum number ($n$), core radius ($r$), and the matching condition between plasmon resonance and exciton resonance frequencies.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the near-field approximation, the use of an averaging method for large excitons, and the assumption of zero confinement potential inside the nanostructure volume for simplified solutions.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the calculated electric field intensity and the averaged local field amplification ($	ilde{\eta}$) as a function of the core radius, highlighting optimal enhancement regions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical interaction (plasmon-exciton coupling) to deriving the necessary mathematical frameworks (Hamiltonians, differential equations like the Whittaker equation) and finally presenting numerical results showing the size-dependent enhancement of quadrupole transitions.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges quantum optics (Rydberg atoms/excitons) with nanophotonics (plasmons), providing a quantitative framework for engineering light-matter interactions to enhance otherwise weak, forbidden transitions.
